# infrawrench_ssh_key (Resource)

An SSH key registered with the organization, in one of two modes.

**Import a key you already hold** by setting `public_key`. Nothing secret enters Terraform, and this is the mode to reach for by default.

**Have the server generate one** by leaving `public_key` unset. The private half is returned exactly once and lands in your state file in plaintext — same warning as `infrawrench_api_key`: only do this with a state backend you would keep any other secret in.

There is no update route. Every attribute forces replacement.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.

### Optional

- `public_key` (String) OpenSSH public key line, e.g. `ssh-ed25519 AAAA… you@host`. Set it to register a key you already have; leave it unset to have one generated, in which case it is filled in from the response.

### Read-Only

- `fingerprint` (String) Key fingerprint, for comparing against what a host reports.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned key id. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `is_imported` (Boolean) `true` when the key was registered rather than generated.
- `key_type` (String) Algorithm, e.g. `ssh-ed25519`. Parsed from the key rather than configured.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The generated private key, in OpenSSH format. Returned **once**, at creation, and not persisted in plaintext server-side.

Null for an imported key, and null after an import into Terraform: nothing can recover it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_ssh_key.example 2b3c4d5e-6f7a-8b9c-0d1e-2f3a4b5c6d7e
```
